title: Speaker or Language? Explaining Variance in Charismatic Prosody Across Luxembourgish and French
abstract: arXiv:2609.16275v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Charismatic speech is shaped by language and speaking style, yet their relative contribution in bilingual public speaking remains unclear. We analyzed spontaneous speeches of 10 politicians who address audiences in Luxembourgish and French, in highly comparable communicative contexts across languages. From 400 utterances, we extracted 41 acoustic-prosodic features linked to vocal charisma and fitted mixed-effects models to separate speaker- and language-related variance. Speaker identity accounted for most variance, whereas language explained less, but still showed systematic differences: French productions showed higher shimmer and phrase-final F0, indicative of a polite, respectful voice, while Luxembourgish productions exhibited stronger mid-frequency spectral energy, suggesting a more vocally present profile. translated_title: 说话人还是语言？解释卢森堡语与法语之间魅力韵律的变异
translated_abstract: 富有魅力的言语受语言和说话方式的影响，但二者在双语公开演讲中的相对贡献仍不清楚。我们分析了10位政治家分别用卢森堡语和法语向听众发表的自发性演讲，这些演讲在跨语言的交际情境上高度可比。我们从400个话语中提取了41个与声音魅力相关的声学-韵律特征，并拟合混合效应模型以分离说话人相关和语言相关的方差。结果表明，说话人身份解释了大部分方差，而语言解释的较少，但仍显示出系统性差异：法语表达显示出更高的微扰（shimmer）和短语末尾基频（F0），表明这是一种礼貌、尊重的声音，而卢森堡语表达则表现出更强的中频谱能量，暗示更具声音存在感的形象。这些模式与卢森堡语作为非正式身份语言、法语作为高声望语言的社会语言学角色相一致。
tldr: 该研究通过分析10位政治家的双语演讲发现，说话人身份是魅力韵律变异的主要来源，但语言本身也产生系统性影响——法语呈现更礼貌尊重的声音特征，卢森堡语则更具声音存在感。
en_tdlr: Analyzing bilingual speeches by 10 politicians, this study finds that speaker identity accounts for most variance in charismatic prosody, yet language still shows systematic effects—French conveys a polite, respectful voice while Luxembourgish presents a more vocally present profile.
